notes: HVS1: prior HVS (Table 1 ref. 1; I:p10-b0, T:p10-b0), explicitly reobserved here (T:p5-b4). HVS2: prior HVS (ref. 2; Hirsch et al. 2005), included in the all-seven Table 1 summary and Fig. 2 but not among the objects listed as reobserved (T:p3-b0, I:p10-b0). HVS3: prior HVS (ref. 3; Edelmann et al. 2005), included in the all-seven Table 1 summary but not listed as reobserved (T:p10-b0, I:p10-b0). HVS4: prior survey HVS from Brown et al. (2006) (ref. 4; I:p10-b0, T:p10-b0), reobserved here (T:p5-b4). HVS5: prior survey HVS from Brown et al. (2006) (ref. 4; I:p10-b0, T:p10-b0), reobserved here (T:p5-b4). HVS6: newly reported and explicitly unbound (T:p3-b7, T:p5-b1). HVS7: newly reported and retained as a probable HVS conditional on the B-main-sequence interpretation; the abstract omits the final '.9' from its catalog identifier, while section 3 and Table 1 give SDSS J113312.12+010824.9 (T:p1-b3, T:p3-b7, T:p4-b6, I:p10-b0). In Table 1, superscript digits after catalog names are reference markers, not identifier characters (I:p10-b0, T:p10-b0).

HVS1: Table 1 (T:p10-b0, mirrored in image I:p10-b0) lists for HVS1 (SDSS J090745.0+024507): l = 227.3 deg, b = 31.3 deg, g' = 19.8, v_RF = +709 km s-1 (no uncertainty), d = 110 kpc, t_GC = 160 Myr. The text (T:p1-b7) reports the same rest-frame velocity as "at least +709 ± 12 km s-1"; the adopted ±12 km s-1 is used here. Per T:p5-b4, v_RF is a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity along the line of sight, not a full space velocity. No explicit J2000 RA/Dec are tabulated for HVS1 (only the SDSS designation, which encodes approximate coordinates), so no position values are recorded. No parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for HVS1.

HVS2: HVS2 is identified as US 708 in Table 1 (catalog entry US 708, reference Hirsch et al. 2005). The paper reports only Galactic coordinates (l, b) = (176.0, 47.1) deg for this star, not equatorial RA/Dec, so no ra or dec values are extracted. Table 1 gives v_RF = +717 km/s, explicitly described as the minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity and not a full space velocity; it is therefore recorded as a lower bound on the Galactic rest-frame speed. No heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS2 in the supplied material. Location T:p10-b0 is a text transcription of Table 1, with the corresponding table image at I:p10-b0.

HVS3: HVS3 (HE 0437-5439) is listed in Table 1 (T:p10-b0). The table reports Galactic coordinates l=263.0 deg and b=-40.9 deg, not equatorial RA/Dec, so no RA or Dec is extracted. Its v_RF value is the paper's minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not a heliocentric radial velocity. No parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

HVS4: HVS4 (SDSS J091301.0+3051204) appears in Table 1. The table lists 75 kpc as a heliocentric distance estimate and +563 km/s as the minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity (explicitly not a full space velocity). No right ascension, declination, parallax, proper motion, heliocentric radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star in the supplied material; Table 2, which contains J2000 coordinates and heliocentric velocities, is only partially reproduced and does not include HVS4. Galactic coordinates l=194.8 deg, b=42.6 deg and g'=18.4 mag are also reported but are not among the requested quantities.

HVS5: The supplied Table 2 excerpt contains only its first three late-B rows, so the HVS5 row with RA/Dec and v_helio is not available in the provided material; I did not infer coordinates or velocity from the catalog identifier. Table 1's v_RF is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame line-of-sight velocity, not a full space velocity, so galactic_rest_frame_velocity is recorded as a lower bound (T:p5-b4, T:p10-b0).

HVS6: Target: HVS6 = SDSS J110557.45+093439.5. RA/Dec are parsed from this SDSS J2000 designation because the supplied Table 2 excerpt does not show the HVS6 row. The paper's v_RF values are explicitly minimum line-of-sight Galactic rest-frame velocities/lower limits to the true space velocity, not full 3D speeds; they are recorded under galactic_rest_frame_velocity with that condition. HVS6 is qualitatively stated to be unbound (T:p5-b1), but no bound/unbound probability, parallax, or proper motion is reported for it.

HVS7: The target is HVS7 = SDSS J113312.12+010824.9. Its J2000 RA/Dec are given only through the SDSS designation (T:p10-b0, T:p3-b7). The paper reports a total proper motion μ = 10.5 ± 9 mas yr−1 for HVS7 (T:p5-b2), but not separate equatorial proper-motion components, so proper_motion_ra and proper_motion_dec are omitted. Distance depends on the adopted interpretation: 55 kpc for a 4 M_sun B7 main-sequence star versus 15 kpc for a BHB star (T:p4-b9, T:p4-b11). The paper calls HVS7 a probable HVS and reports no bound/unbound probability.
